t: You're looking at number fifteen, Kensington Palace Gardens, a grand house in one of London's most exclusive streets. It was commissioned by George Moore, an English lace merchant and philanthropist born in Mealsgate, Cumberland. Moore built up great wealth, and this mansion was built for him. The architect was James Thomas Knowles the elder, who designed it. Moore later moved back to Mealsgate, so the house stands as a record of his success in London.
